title: Outlook: usage display for Recoverable Items storage
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned storage display and the existing Exchange controls. Minor corrections should distinguish legacy portal guidance, qualify the quotas when archiving is enabled, and acknowledge the published product-level licensing requirement.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Get-MailboxFolderStatistics -Identity <mailbox> -FolderScope RecoverableItems retrieves the mailbox's Recoverable Items folder statistics.
claims.quote: RecoverableItems: Returns output for the Recoverable Items folder and the Deletions, DiscoveryHolds, Purges, and Versions subfolders.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Get-EXOMailboxFolderStatistics instead in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: In Exchange Online PowerShell, we recommend that you use the Get-EXOMailboxFolderStatistics cmdlet instead of this cmdlet.

claims.claim: The -Archive switch retrieves the archive mailbox's usage statistics.
claims.quote: The Archive switch specifies whether to return the usage statistics of the archive associated with the mailbox or mail user.

claims.claim: Exchange admin center > Compliance management > Retention policies is the cited route for the archive-move retention policy.
claims.quote: In the EAC, go to Compliance management > Retention policies, and then select Add
claims.fix: Retain the route only with this qualification in the row note: 'The cited article gives this legacy EAC policy route; Recoverable Items folder in Exchange Online says Exchange security and compliance features are no longer available in the new EAC. This path reaches the policies page, not tag creation or mailbox assignment.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/security-and-compliance/recoverable-items-folder/recoverable-items-folder.

claims.claim: New-RetentionPolicyTag -Name <Name of RPT> -Type RecoverableItems -AgeLimitForRetention <Number of days> -RetentionAction MoveToArchive creates a Recoverable Items archive-move tag.
claims.quote: New-RetentionPolicyTag -Name <Name of RPT> -Type RecoverableItems -AgeLimitForRetention <Number of days> -RetentionAction MoveToArchive

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The cited existing retention-tag control is described for moving aged Recoverable Items of mailboxes on hold to the archive.
claims.quote: This RPT moves items from the Recoverable Items folder in the user's primary mailbox to the Recoverable Items folder in the user's archive mailbox.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls; Why it matters
claims.claim: Moving these items to the archive requires the archive mailbox to be enabled; otherwise no action is taken.
claims.quote: For this process to work, the user's archive mailbox must be enabled. If the archive mailbox isn't enabled, no action is taken

claims.claim: The Recoverable Items retention tag must be created in PowerShell, not in the Exchange admin center.
claims.quote: Use PowerShell to create an RPT for the Recoverable Items folder. You can't use the Exchange admin center (EAC).

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said the existing statistics and archive controls change what the new display shows.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Recoverable Items storage usage display location archive subfolders rollout default. Read Get-MailboxFolderStatistics and Increase the Recoverable Items quota for mailboxes on hold; neither describes an effect on the new Outlook display.

claims.claim: Recoverable Items resides in a hidden, non-IPM part of the mailbox that Outlook users cannot browse.
claims.quote: The Recoverable Items folder resides in the non-IPM subtree of each mailbox. This subtree isn't visible to users using Outlook, Outlook on the web (formerly known as Outlook Web App), or other email clients.
